previous_mapping.record_grain: One row per (ip_right_type, application_number, party_id, party_role) party-role involvement record
previous_mapping.grain_rationale: The header defines 14 columns covering right type, application, party identity (party_id, abn), role (category and role), party type/name, address codes, activity dates and is_current/is_founding flags. The same party_id can appear on multiple applications and in multiple roles, and the same application can carry multiple parties, so no single column is a unique key; the natural grain is one party-role involvement per application.

record_id.rationale: No single column is unique; the party-role row is identified by a deterministic content hash over the raw record, traceable back to the exact raw row.

fields.rationale: ip_right_type is the published IP right family; mapped to the new ip_application right_type enum, with unlisted families falling to 'other' rather than being guessed.
application_number is the IP Australia application identifier; kept as published and qualified by right_type, not treated as a party or company identifier.
party_id is the IP Australia party identifier; kept as a party attribute and never treated as or converted into an ABN.

party_name is the published party name; it may be an organisation, a personal name or a numeric-looking string, so it is kept as a party name and not promoted to a business legal name. Marked personal_data=always because the population mixes individuals.
party_type distinguishes organisation and individual parties; mapped to the party kind enum with unknown for unlisted values, and never used to infer sole trader or company legal form.
party_role_category is the coarse published role level; kept distinct from the finer party_role and not collapsed into it.
party_role is the finer published role (patentee, applicant, agent, opponent_agent); applicant, patentee and agent roles are not interchangeable and are kept as published.
is_current is a party-activity currency flag; mapped to the party concept, not to entity.status, because it does not establish company status or IP right enforceability.
is_founding is a supplied party-activity attribute; kept as a party flag and explicitly not read as company founding or incorporation evidence.

abn is an optional party attribute, blank in most sampled rows; checksum-validated with the abn transform and never derived from party_id or party_name. Owned by ip_party because the party may be an individual or agent, not necessarily the subject business.

state_code is the raw state/territory code of the party address; kept as published on the party record rather than normalised into the business address.state enum, since it may be non-Australian or blank and is not a jurisdiction of incorporation.
post_code is a heterogeneous party-address field (e.g. 't6b 3n9', '110044'); kept exactly as recorded on the party record and not normalised through the AU postcode transform.
country_code is the lower-case country code of the party address; kept as published on the party record and not read as a company jurisdiction of incorporation.
effective_from_date dates when the party-activity claim became true; mapped to the generic observation.valid_from facet, not to a business incorporation or licence start date.

effective_to_date dates when the party-activity claim stopped being true; mapped to observation.valid_to, where null means still current as far as this source knows. It is not a licence end or business end date.

ip_application.rationale: An IP application is identified by right type plus application number; the number alone is not unique across right types.

ip_party.rationale: The party is identified by the IP Australia party_id; it is not necessarily a business or a company.

relationships.rationale: Each party-role row records that the party appears on that IP application in the stated role; the edge is emitted only when both roles have emitted claims.

previous_mapping.notes: All 15 source columns are consumed: 13 map to new ip_party/ip_application concepts, and effective_from_date/effective_to_date map to the generic observation.valid_from/valid_to facets. Validity is expressed per claim, not as a record-wide rule: effective_from_date and effective_to_date are each mapped as their own field rule onto the observation.valid_from/valid_to facets, so every party-role claim carries its own validity window and no record-wide validity_date_formats or valid_from/valid_to path is declared on any other field. No subject business role is declared because the source does not establish a business subject; party records may be individuals or agents. party_id is never treated as an ABN, and abn is checksum-validated. is_current and is_founding are party-activity flags, not company status or incorporation evidence. Address codes are kept raw on the party record and are not normalised geography or incorporation jurisdiction. This is a 25,000-record prefix cohort, so no population-level uniqueness or coverage claims are made. Confidence values are mapping-policy scores, not calibrated probabilities.

entity_types.name: ip_application
entity_types.definition: An IP Australia application/registration identified by ip_right_type plus application_number; a right record, not a party and not a company.

entity_types.name: ip_party
entity_types.definition: A party recorded by IP Australia on an IP application (organisation, individual or agent), identified by party_id. Not necessarily a business and not necessarily a company.

concepts.definition: The IP right family the application_number belongs to, as published (e.g. patent). Qualifies the application number, which is not unique across right types.
concepts.why_not_existing: No existing concept describes an IP right family; entity.industry_code and licence concepts describe business activity or authorisations, not IP application types.

concepts.definition: IP Australia application number as published. Identifies the application only together with the right type; it is not a party or company identifier.
concepts.why_not_existing: Existing identifiers cover businesses (abn, acn, nzbn) and licences (ext.licence.number); none identifies an IP application.

concepts.definition: IP Australia party identifier for a party on an application. Separate from any ABN; must not be treated as or converted into an ABN.
concepts.why_not_existing: No existing concept holds a publisher party identifier; entity.abn/acn are business numbers with checksums and are not interchangeable with party_id.

concepts.definition: Party name as published by IP Australia. May be an organisation name, a personal name or a numeric-looking string; it is not evidence of legal form or company status.
concepts.why_not_existing: entity.legal_name asserts a registered legal name of a business, which this field does not establish; party names include individuals and agents and must not be promoted to legal names.

concepts.definition: Whether IP Australia records the party as an organisation or an individual. Matching evidence only; never implies sole trader or company legal form.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.holder_kind is owned by business and describes a licence/registration holder; reusing it would assert a business subject that this party record does not establish.

concepts.definition: Coarse party-role category as published (applicant, applicant_agent, opposition_agent, mortgagee ...). Distinct from the finer party_role and must not be collapsed into it.
concepts.why_not_existing: No existing concept describes a party's role on an IP application; licence concepts describe authorisations held, not procedural roles.

concepts.definition: Finer party role as published (patentee, applicant, agent, opponent_agent ...). Applicant, patentee and agent roles are not interchangeable.
concepts.why_not_existing: No existing concept captures procedural party roles on an IP application; ext.licence.grade describes licence kinds, not application roles.

concepts.definition: Whether the party-activity record is current as published. Does not establish that the IP right is enforceable or that the party still exists.
concepts.why_not_existing: entity.status is a business lifecycle status (active, deregistered ...) and would misstate a party-activity flag as company status.

concepts.definition: The is_founding flag as supplied on the party-activity record. It is a party-activity attribute and must not be read as company founding or incorporation evidence.
concepts.why_not_existing: ext.entity.date_established records a founding date; no existing concept holds this boolean activity flag, and reusing establishment concepts would imply incorporation evidence.

concepts.definition: ABN supplied for the party where present. Blank in most sampled rows; must be checksum-validated and never derived from party_id or party_name.
concepts.why_not_existing: entity.abn is owned by business and asserts the subject business's ABN; here the ABN is an optional attribute of a party that may be an individual or agent, so ownership differs.

concepts.definition: State/territory code of the party address as recorded (e.g. vic, qld). Raw publisher value, not normalised geography and not a jurisdiction of incorporation.
concepts.why_not_existing: address.state is an enum owned by business with a fixed value set and would force normalisation; this raw party-address code belongs to the party record and may be non-Australian or blank.

concepts.definition: Post code of the party address exactly as recorded, including non-Australian formats (e.g. 't6b 3n9', '110044'). Not normalised.
concepts.why_not_existing: address.postcode is owned by business and implies a normalised business address; this value is a heterogeneous party-address field that cannot be normalised without loss.

concepts.definition: Lower-case country code of the party address as recorded (e.g. us, hk, in). Describes the party address, not a company jurisdiction of incorporation.
concepts.why_not_existing: address.country is owned by business and would assert the business's country; this is a raw party-address code that must not be read as incorporation jurisdiction.

relationships.name: PARTY_ON_APPLICATION
relationships.definition: The party is recorded by IP Australia on this IP application in the role stated on the party-role record.

reuse.observation.source_id: Identifies the IP RAPID party_activity dataset the claim came from.
reuse.observation.source_record_id: Content-hash record identifier for the party-role row, traceable to the raw record.
reuse.observation.observed_at: Observation-at-retrieval timestamp from the snapshot metadata.
reuse.observation.valid_from: Per-claim validity start: effective_from_date is mapped as its own field rule onto this facet, so each party-role claim carries its own validity start rather than a record-wide rule.
reuse.observation.valid_to: Per-claim validity end: effective_to_date is mapped as its own field rule onto this facet, so each party-role claim carries its own validity end; null means still current as far as this source knows.
reuse.confidence.field_confidence: Records mapping certainty for the party-role row.

unmapped.reason: Mapped to the generic observation.valid_from as an explicit per-claim validity start on each party-role claim, not a record-wide validity rule and not a business or licence date; no new concept is proposed to avoid duplicating the observation facet.
Mapped to the generic observation.valid_to as an explicit per-claim validity end on each party-role claim, not a record-wide validity rule and not a licence end or business end.
